SPN-087 removes the obsolete rail/sidebar fixture implementation left behind by the production Storybook migrations. The retired screen import island and its private styles are unreachable; the only retained import of `mockups.css` was the shared Controls specimen.

- Delete 12 unused prototype TSX files, seven private CSS files, and the 1,966-line `mockups.css`.
- Preserve the four effective Controls layout selectors and existing 640px padding breakpoint in the plain, 33-line `controlsStories.css`.
- Preserve production Dashboard, EditorFrame, Space, profile, administration, guest states, shared Controls/ThemeMenu, entry styles, all native fixtures and all **1,041 stable story IDs**. The 16 retained `redesign-*` IDs keep their current production/native titles.
- Add an actual same-document Appearance → Controls → Appearance regression. Loading the old stylesheet changed the nested icon picker from block to grid, increased its height by 57px, and changed the selected cover border. The check compares production geometry/styles, verifies document identity and runtime errors, and uses existing readiness and failure diagnostics.
- Remove only SPN-087, append it to `grooming.completed_since`, verify no dependent tickets remain, and regenerate the backlog index.

No production component, permission, navigation, server, token, dependency or design behavior changes. Owners, Collaborators, Operators and Link guests retain their actual production surfaces and access boundaries. There are no remaining visible Redesign examples owned by this ticket.

Feedback is retained and counts against the scan budget; deletion and exact logical-byte accounting commit together. No new index must fit before a full store can recover. a view-only Doc currently sends an automatic header/footer field refresh through native edit permissions, producing a protection warning before the command can do nothing. This draft refuses only that initialization request for the exact unit and live viewer grant through Univer's public command-service override. Explicit refresh, real edits, other units and collaboration mutations keep their native behavior.

**Draft and unaccepted.** Source **b9e57e465727870542177170b9acdc56656584ab**, base **18a8759c498574a1d9cc24a969a558cd97a798ed**. Proposed ticket removal/index updates are landing preparation only; SPN-106 remains open on main.

## Coverage and review

- Native permission controls cover member/guest viewers, the unguarded warning, unchanged content, synchronous/asynchronous startup, explicit refresh and real edit denial, other-unit delegation, upgrade and downgrade.
- Existing document browser tests add plain and stale header/footer date-field snapshots, account/guest viewers, desktop/390px load and reload, pre-navigation warning history, persisted snapshot integrity, the account HTTP write fence, an authorized concurrent editor and guest revocation.
- PDF Export and guest-link tests retain their own assertions and now catch startup notices before they can disappear.
- Existing native phone stories record permission errors before document creation. The new ViewerDeniedEdit story calls the mounted public Doc API, requires a false edit result and unchanged native body/layout, and checks one real permission event plus the visible protection warning. No new design pattern or Redesign example is introduced.
- Existing broad source/shared-dependency routing remains; no worker, retry, threshold or assertion was removed.

Both independent full-source reviewers found the unfocused browser pseudo-edit insufficient. Commit b9e57e46 removes it and adds the meaningful native denial story above. Reviewer B cleared that repair; Reviewer A's revalidation is pending. The public override has no identified production-source blocker. **Agent review only; no final grades or visual approval yet.**

## Validation

Passed locally under the shared serial watchdog: formatting, scoped Oxlint, backlog validation, exact-title PR check and strict scoped TypeScript for the permission implementation/native tests and changed browser/stories. The type checks took 1,176 ms / 147.6 MiB and 641 ms / 527.0 MiB sampled peak respectively. These are not runtime passes.

Runtime is **not yet verified**. Two private npm installs were resource-aborted when system memory pressure rose. A private APFS clone of an existing complete installation with identical manifest/lockfile and postinstall scripts succeeded. The focused native-permission suite was then resource-aborted before any test result. No aborted workload is counted as passing; further heavy local execution is deferred. [Preserved local evidence](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/b9e57e465727870542177170b9acdc56656584ab/docs/implementation/evidence/SPN-106-local.json).

Why

Sheets could display stored images but account editors could not add their own. This change makes the native **Insert → Image → Float Image / Cell Image** flow usable, including external image-file paste and drop, while preserving saved bytes, collaboration and native editing.

**Reviewed head:** `eb72be12e3ef774bd8f5938010f193db5b289516`  
**Base:** `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b`  
The requested outcome is an open, mergeable PR; leave it unmerged.

## What changes

- Reuse the existing item-scoped PNG/JPEG/WebP upload route and its decoding, sanitization, deduplication and limits: **5 MiB/file, 16 megapixels, 50 MiB retained/document**.
- Await the entire native insertion, including image decoding and its drawing/cell mutation. Saving, navigation and refresh protection remain active until it settles; closing the editor cancels outstanding work.
- Capture the target before the chooser opens and recheck selection, cell content, worksheet structure and current edit authority before a late insertion. Refuse a changed target or lost access with a useful retry message.
- Preserve native Undo/Redo, movement, cut/paste, worksheet duplication, live peer delivery, reload and named history. A small public render interceptor copies cell-image layout input because Univer's nested display mutation otherwise changed authored content, triggered a sync divergence and discarded Undo.
- Allow new uploads for account editors only, preserving ordinary-item and exact Space-child access. Existing Doc guest uploads and authorized operations on existing Sheet content retain their behavior.
- Use the existing fixed 44 px help slot and DetailsPopover for readable keyboard/touch errors. New insertion requires a connection; newly inserted bytes in a downloaded Sheet remain available after offline reload.

No new package, proprietary package, image store, synchronization model or SDK patch.

Problem and result

An interrupted restore can leave the workspace closed even though its newest original content is preserved. This PR adds the supported `recover-original --operation UUID` supervisor command to authenticate that original, reconcile access and negative restore evidence, and open it as a new original generation. It preserves work saved after the last backup and reports the existing **Original content was recovered** outcome/banner.

## Implementation and safety

- Fresh, bounded cold-host Operator authority comes from the existing private service-UID control socket. The expired application authorization, original restore intent and every interrupted cold attempt remain immutable history.
- Recovery verifies the frozen source against the independent pre-shutdown fingerprint, retains the closed live tuple as private raw evidence, and reuses rollback reconciliation, the prepared-original installer and the original private-trial commitment protocol.
- Partial replacement bytes are never opened as SQLite. Missing, changed, ambiguous, wrong-target or wrong-policy evidence leaves the workspace closed.
- A committed backup is never replaced. A committed original can reopen its current live generation without reinstalling older bytes; replay cannot take over a different maintenance operation.
- The maintained backup and maintenance runbooks describe the supported command and limits. SPN-124's lifetime extension and SPN-125's evidence pruning remain separate.

## Scope and current checkpoint

Draft while real-process acceptance, full CI and final independent reviews are in progress. Published implementation candidate: `a8d326c24d13b53d4f35857c73c50331714b4c41`; base: `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b`. The complete L outcome and all four persona effects are recorded in `docs/implementation/SPN-128.md`. No new visual layout or interaction state is introduced; the existing recovered outcome/banner is exercised by the crash harness.

## Validation checkpoint — not final acceptance

Local checks use Node 26.12.1, the shared serial test lock and the required 2 GiB / 475-second process-tree watchdog.

| Check | Current evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Original/cold/failed custody tests | 95/95 passed; 574.7 MiB peak; 37.2 seconds |
| Cold recovery journal tests | 17/17 passed; 418.1 MiB peak; 30.68 seconds including lock wait |
| Integrated typecheck | Passed; 1,841.5 MiB peak; 185.63 seconds including lock wait |
| Real-process SIGKILL acceptance | Running: required historical cuts plus the new command's admission, preparation, activation, private opening and commitment cuts |
| Current-candidate CI | [CI run 41343337417](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41343337417) queued; other applicable workflows are also running/queued |
| Independent reviews | Source review underway; two final nonimplementing rubric reviews on the same final SHA remain pending |

Initial validation exposed a state-fixture directory layout error and a TypeScript type-predicate narrowing error; both were repaired and the affected checks passed. Independent source inspection found a stale terminal-command replay could take over later maintenance; an exact-operation guard and process regression were added. A sandbox-only custody run lacked valid process-tree memory accounting and is superseded by the host-watchdog run above.

The crash harness uses actual SIGKILL and supervisor restart. Expired authorization is exercised with a test-controlled clock; this is not a wall-clock soak claim. Source fingerprints and reconciled-output fingerprints are deliberately distinct because reconciliation revokes sessions/capabilities and rotates generation evidence.

## Landing intent

Complete all seven required CI gates, applicable additional checks, real-process acceptance and both independent reviews before marking ready. Leave this PR open and unmerged as requested.

Why

SPN-099 removes the temporary core SDK repair while preserving concurrent Doc editing, native history, link identity and clean installs. This PR implements the renewed single-ticket request. It remains unmerged.

## What changes

- All 23 direct `@univerjs/*` package names across the app/workspaces stay aligned at the published **1.1.0** release. Core ES/CJS builds are verified against their complete official SHA-256 values after installation. The core installer, its obsolete tests, postinstall command and live documentation references are removed.
- `@spinel/sync-transform` installs a shared public native boundary in browser editors, snapshot viewers, confirmed replicas, server models and native test harnesses. Actual custom-range state stays canonical through edits, publication and Undo/Redo.
- The native hyperlink producer's exact local overlapping-retain shape is repaired before command application. Remote, sync-only, mixed-content and opaque shapes retain their existing validation path.
- A DI factory creates the **same exported native Docs manager** with a composed optional UI interceptor. Desktop/mobile IME provider behavior and metadata are preserved. Only paragraph REPLACE retains need isolated history; ordinary typing and Enter keep existing grouping and bounded history.
- The transform layer preserves explicit falsy replacement style keys and explicit empty paragraph intent through slicing across unstyled retains and insertion boundaries. This is not a claim of convergence for every arbitrary paragraph-body conflict. Temporary slice markers cannot reach native apply or the wire.
- The independent Docs composition, UI resize, drawing refresh and Docs UI callback guards remain in place. Their regression suites and retained-drawing/browser obligations remain applicable.

The remaining paragraph REPLACE composition, explicit empty iterator slice, and falsy text-style ownership fixes have been submitted as [Univer PR #7987](https://github.com/dream-num/univer/pull/7987), head `b066a6279beac38db1b0d32377bfbc98d6f32bc7`, against upstream dev `4e6a56e45c8647d9741139af7ebf2f725945d7f3`. The contribution is open and unmerged; it does not establish that a published SDK contains these fixes.

The official **1.3.1** audit still found the relevant core defect forms, and [upstream PR #7938](https://github.com/dream-num/univer/pull/7938) remains open. Qualifying unchanged 1.1.0 through the ticket's stock-behavior adaptation rule avoids coupling core removal to an unrelated drawing/offline SDK upgrade. This PR does **not** claim a newer SDK migration.

Implementation decisions, all four persona effects, old-to-new regression coverage and precise native/IME evidence scope are maintained in [SPN-099.md](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/f4e7db978a553a0dcc286937503de87b79ee9d06/docs/implementation/SPN-099.md).

## Verification checkpoint

Main advanced with SPN-112 during qualification. This candidate preserves both parent histories and both tickets' completion records. The only merge conflicts were the backlog source/index; the index was regenerated under the watchdog (0.69 s / 125.0 MiB). No SPN-099 production/test changes were needed. Source inspection confirms the restore paths use the same adapted native model; current-head CI must validate the combined app and its new unit partitions/supervised-restore project.

The immediately preceding `76aafdf` head could not start pull-request CI while its backlog conflicted with new main. That conflict is resolved here.

Local diagnostics use host Node **24.22.1**. The officially verified Node 26.12.1 binary crashes before startup on this host; hosted CI uses the repository-pinned runtime and remains the acceptance gate. Local runs use the serial runner and a process-tree 2 GiB/eight-minute watchdog.

### Failure dispositions and limits

The first runtime checkpoint `98bb7db` ([CI run](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41326551744)) exposed formatting/test-type errors, duplicate UI interceptor registration and over-broad paragraph history isolation. These were corrected in the current candidate; that failed run is not counted as final acceptance. Its four library partitions passed, while Unit and browser gates correctly rejected the checkpoint.

Two new adversarial fixtures reproduced pre-existing stock behavior outside captured native producer shapes: arbitrary paragraph-style COVER and a combined paragraph/comment REPLACE. The full **L, pre-launch** outcome retains editor-independent Doc/Sheet replay, exact account/item authority and revocation, exclusive writer ownership, persisted snapshot/outbox acknowledgement, exactly-once retry, interruption/recovery, separate-viewer content and a bounded installed-phone observation. Closed-app OS background execution, periodic polling, unrelated offline image/creation changes and iPhone acceptance remain outside this ticket.

[Original ticket](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/c525aa933505d6e78b8fdd7a89940d87506d5cb3/docs/todo/SPN-156.md), [canonical decisions and complete evidence](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/5c764793f03f7f885873d08d6eca0660cd401bf0/docs/implementation/SPN-156.md), [complete base/source diff](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/compare/c525aa933505d6e78b8fdd7a89940d87506d5cb3...5c764793f03f7f885873d08d6eca0660cd401bf0).

All four personas informed the design. Owner gets durable delivery and foreground priority; Collaborator retains the existing account/access/revocation path and recoverable work; Operator gets bounded native concurrency and inspectable cleanup using existing components; Link guest receives no private replay owner or account store. Lost-ack attention remains conservative. Background replay cannot silently publish a recovery copy. This connects existing pending/saved/attention states; no new visual component, layout/theme change or routine screenshot matrix is introduced. 🧩 Scope and resulting behavior

SPN-087 removes the obsolete rail/sidebar fixture implementation left behind by the production Storybook migrations. The retired screen import island and its private styles are unreachable; the only retained import of `mockups.css` was the shared Controls specimen.

- Delete 12 unused prototype TSX files, seven private CSS files, and the 1,966-line `mockups.css`.
- Preserve the four effective Controls layout selectors and existing 640px padding breakpoint in the plain, 33-line `controlsStories.css`.
- Preserve production Dashboard, EditorFrame, Space, profile, administration, guest states, shared Controls/ThemeMenu, entry styles, all native fixtures and all **1,041 stable story IDs**. The 16 retained `redesign-*` IDs keep their current production/native titles.
- Add an actual same-document Appearance → Controls → Appearance regression. Loading the old stylesheet changed the nested icon picker from block to grid, increased its height by 57px, and changed the selected cover border. The check compares production geometry/styles, verifies document identity and runtime errors, and uses existing readiness and failure diagnostics.
- Remove only SPN-087, append it to `grooming.completed_since`, verify no dependent tickets remain, and regenerate the backlog index.

No production component, permission, navigation, server, token, dependency or design behavior changes. Owners, Collaborators, Operators and Link guests retain their actual production surfaces and access boundaries. There are no remaining visible Redesign examples owned by this ticket.

**Size:** 14,013 counted changed lines, chiefly the coherent obsolete-source deletion and preserved evidence. The maintained [implementation record](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/0ed9ef8b23bccbae4f24f4b608a6b55b54c47526/docs/implementation/SPN-087.md) explains the soft-limit decision and inventory. 💬 Why and what changes

SPN-089 completes the title-cue audit across **45 production dialog owners** and corrects the vertical icon offset reported in review.

- The shared `Modal` requires exactly one explicit semantic `icon` or literal `emoji`, alongside its textual title.
- `ModalTitleContent` supplies the native formula dialog, Profile/Appearance picker, Space contents drawer and SDK Make a copy title.
- The decorative cue centers inside the title's **first line-height**, including wrapped headings. The competing Profile heading rule is removed. Storybook checks actual SVG/emoji bounds against the first text line within 1 CSS pixel after fonts load.
- Textual accessible names, keyboard/focus behavior, pending-operation handling, native SDK ownership and permissions remain part of acceptance.

a view-only Doc currently sends an automatic header/footer field refresh through native edit permissions, producing a protection warning before the command can do nothing. This draft refuses only that initialization request for the exact unit and live viewer grant through Univer's public command-service override. Explicit refresh, real edits, other units and collaboration mutations keep their native behavior.

**Draft and unaccepted.** Source **b9e57e465727870542177170b9acdc56656584ab**, base **18a8759c498574a1d9cc24a969a558cd97a798ed**. Proposed ticket removal/index updates are landing preparation only; SPN-106 remains open on main.

## Coverage and review

- Native permission controls cover member/guest viewers, the unguarded warning, unchanged content, synchronous/asynchronous startup, explicit refresh and real edit denial, other-unit delegation, upgrade and downgrade.
- Existing document browser tests add plain and stale header/footer date-field snapshots, account/guest viewers, desktop/390px load and reload, pre-navigation warning history, persisted snapshot integrity, the account HTTP write fence, an authorized concurrent editor and guest revocation.
- PDF Export and guest-link tests retain their own assertions and now catch startup notices before they can disappear.
- Existing native phone stories record permission errors before document creation. The new ViewerDeniedEdit story calls the mounted public Doc API, requires a false edit result and unchanged native body/layout, and checks one real permission event plus the visible protection warning. No new design pattern or Redesign example is introduced.
- Existing broad source/shared-dependency routing remains; no worker, retry, threshold or assertion was removed.

Both independent full-source reviewers found the unfocused browser pseudo-edit insufficient. Commit b9e57e46 removes it and adds the meaningful native denial story above. Reviewer B cleared that repair; Reviewer A's revalidation is pending. The public override has no identified production-source blocker. **Agent review only; no final grades or visual approval yet.**

## Validation

Passed locally under the shared serial watchdog: formatting, scoped Oxlint, backlog validation, exact-title PR check and strict scoped TypeScript for the permission implementation/native tests and changed browser/stories. The type checks took 1,176 ms / 147.6 MiB and 641 ms / 527.0 MiB sampled peak respectively. These are not runtime passes.

Runtime is **not yet verified**. Two private npm installs were resource-aborted when system memory pressure rose. A private APFS clone of an existing complete installation with identical manifest/lockfile and postinstall scripts succeeded. The focused native-permission suite was then resource-aborted before any test result. No aborted workload is counted as passing; further heavy local execution is deferred. [Preserved local evidence](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/b9e57e465727870542177170b9acdc56656584ab/docs/implementation/evidence/SPN-106-local.json).

## Remaining before merge

Current required CI, real startup/field persistence and denial/revocation results, PDF/guest-link regressions, actual light/dark/phone screenshots embedded here, independent visual approval and two independent scores above 95 on the same accepted commit. Screenshots are planned, not yet captured.

Why

Sheets could display stored images but account editors could not add their own. This change makes the native **Insert → Image → Float Image / Cell Image** flow usable, including external image-file paste and drop, while preserving saved bytes, collaboration and native editing.

**Reviewed head:** `eb72be12e3ef774bd8f5938010f193db5b289516`  
**Base:** `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b`  
The requested outcome is an open, mergeable PR; leave it unmerged.

## What changes

- Reuse the existing item-scoped PNG/JPEG/WebP upload route and its decoding, sanitization, deduplication and limits: **5 MiB/file, 16 megapixels, 50 MiB retained/document**.
- Await the entire native insertion, including image decoding and its drawing/cell mutation. Saving, navigation and refresh protection remain active until it settles; closing the editor cancels outstanding work.
- Capture the target before the chooser opens and recheck selection, cell content, worksheet structure and current edit authority before a late insertion. Refuse a changed target or lost access with a useful retry message.
- Preserve native Undo/Redo, movement, cut/paste, worksheet duplication, live peer delivery, reload and named history. A small public render interceptor copies cell-image layout input because Univer's nested display mutation otherwise changed authored content, triggered a sync divergence and discarded Undo.
- Allow new uploads for account editors only, preserving ordinary-item and exact Space-child access. Existing Doc guest uploads and authorized operations on existing Sheet content retain their behavior.
- Use the existing fixed 44 px help slot and DetailsPopover for readable keyboard/touch errors. New insertion requires a connection; newly inserted bytes in a downloaded Sheet remain available after offline reload.

No new package, proprietary package, image store, synchronization model or SDK patch.

The native cohort exercises both menu placements and Undo/Redo, peer delivery, reload/history, row movement, native cut/paste and worksheet duplication, PNG paste/WebP drop/JPEG phone chooser, oversize refusal, navigation protection during decoding, native phone menu and details, changed-selection refusal/retry, viewer/guest/offline refusal, chooser cancellation plus peer structure changes, **access downgrade after upload**, and **online insertion into an already downloaded Sheet followed by offline reload**. Page errors and any sync resync fail the cohort.

Native application/test source was frozen at `6908f392da45217fc63dbb146b7f66a191ff5365`. The only later executable change awaits asynchronous focus return in two Storybook assertions; the exact focus expectations are preserved. Per-file hashes in the durable record establish unchanged application/test source at the reviewed head.

Local workloads used the repository serial lock and **2 GiB process-tree watchdog**. The native run used Node 26.12.1, Playwright 1.64.1/Chromium 156 build 1248, one worker, zero retries and local Chromium heap limits. Early browser/full-Storybook memory aborts and heap OOMs are recorded as unsuccessful attempts. The full catalogue built in CI; a narrowed local build of the real production stories supplied the focused checks. Phone captures use Chromium touch emulation; physical-device acceptance remains SPN-090.

Problem and result

An interrupted restore can leave the workspace closed even though its newest original content is preserved. This PR adds the supported `recover-original --operation UUID` supervisor command to authenticate that original, reconcile access and negative restore evidence, and open it as a new original generation. It preserves work saved after the last backup and reports the existing **Original content was recovered** outcome/banner.

## Implementation and safety

- Fresh, bounded cold-host Operator authority comes from the existing private service-UID control socket. The expired application authorization, original restore intent and every interrupted cold attempt remain immutable history.
- Recovery verifies the frozen source against the independent pre-shutdown fingerprint, retains the closed live tuple as private raw evidence, and reuses rollback reconciliation, the prepared-original installer and the original private-trial commitment protocol.
- Partial replacement bytes are never opened as SQLite. Missing, changed, ambiguous, wrong-target or wrong-policy evidence leaves the workspace closed.
- A committed backup is never replaced. A committed original can reopen its current live generation without reinstalling older bytes; replay cannot take over a different maintenance operation.
- The maintained backup and maintenance runbooks describe the supported command and limits. SPN-124's lifetime extension and SPN-125's evidence pruning remain separate.

## Scope and current checkpoint

Draft while real-process acceptance, full CI and final independent reviews are in progress. Published implementation candidate: `a8d326c24d13b53d4f35857c73c50331714b4c41`; base: `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b`. The complete L outcome and all four persona effects are recorded in `docs/implementation/SPN-128.md`. No new visual layout or interaction state is introduced; the existing recovered outcome/banner is exercised by the crash harness.

## Validation checkpoint — not final acceptance

Local checks use Node 26.12.1, the shared serial test lock and the required 2 GiB / 475-second process-tree watchdog.

| Check | Current evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Original/cold/failed custody tests | 95/95 passed; 574.7 MiB peak; 37.2 seconds |
| Cold recovery journal tests | 17/17 passed; 418.1 MiB peak; 30.68 seconds including lock wait |
| Integrated typecheck | Passed; 1,841.5 MiB peak; 185.63 seconds including lock wait |
| Real-process SIGKILL acceptance | Running: required historical cuts plus the new command's admission, preparation, activation, private opening and commitment cuts |
| Current-candidate CI | [CI run 41343337417](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41343337417) queued; other applicable workflows are also running/queued |
| Independent reviews | Source review underway; two final nonimplementing rubric reviews on the same final SHA remain pending |

Initial validation exposed a state-fixture directory layout error and a TypeScript type-predicate narrowing error; both were repaired and the affected checks passed. Independent source inspection found a stale terminal-command replay could take over later maintenance; an exact-operation guard and process regression were added. A sandbox-only custody run lacked valid process-tree memory accounting and is superseded by the host-watchdog run above.

The crash harness uses actual SIGKILL and supervisor restart. Expired authorization is exercised with a test-controlled clock; this is not a wall-clock soak claim. Source fingerprints and reconciled-output fingerprints are deliberately distinct because reconciliation revokes sessions/capabilities and rotates generation evidence.

## Landing intent

Complete all seven required CI gates, applicable additional checks, real-process acceptance and both independent reviews before marking ready. Leave this PR open and unmerged as requested.

Why

SPN-099 removes the temporary core SDK repair while preserving concurrent Doc editing, native history, link identity and clean installs. This PR implements the renewed single-ticket request. It remains unmerged.

## What changes

- All 23 direct `@univerjs/*` package names across the app/workspaces stay aligned at the published **1.1.0** release. Core ES/CJS builds are verified against their complete official SHA-256 values after installation. The core installer, its obsolete tests, postinstall command and live documentation references are removed.
- `@spinel/sync-transform` installs a shared public native boundary in browser editors, snapshot viewers, confirmed replicas, server models and native test harnesses. Actual custom-range state stays canonical through edits, publication and Undo/Redo.
- The native hyperlink producer's exact local overlapping-retain shape is repaired before command application. Remote, sync-only, mixed-content and opaque shapes retain their existing validation path.
- A DI factory creates the **same exported native Docs manager** with a composed optional UI interceptor. Desktop/mobile IME provider behavior and metadata are preserved. Only paragraph REPLACE retains need isolated history; ordinary typing and Enter keep existing grouping and bounded history.
- The transform layer preserves explicit falsy replacement style keys and explicit empty paragraph intent through slicing across unstyled retains and insertion boundaries. This is not a claim of convergence for every arbitrary paragraph-body conflict. Temporary slice markers cannot reach native apply or the wire.
- The independent Docs composition, UI resize, drawing refresh and Docs UI callback guards remain in place. Their regression suites and retained-drawing/browser obligations remain applicable.

The remaining paragraph REPLACE composition, explicit empty iterator slice, and falsy text-style ownership fixes have been submitted as [Univer PR #7987](https://github.com/dream-num/univer/pull/7987), head `b066a6279beac38db1b0d32377bfbc98d6f32bc7`, against upstream dev `4e6a56e45c8647d9741139af7ebf2f725945d7f3`. The contribution is open and unmerged; it does not establish that a published SDK contains these fixes.

The official **1.3.1** audit still found the relevant core defect forms, and [upstream PR #7938](https://github.com/dream-num/univer/pull/7938) remains open. Qualifying unchanged 1.1.0 through the ticket's stock-behavior adaptation rule avoids coupling core removal to an unrelated drawing/offline SDK upgrade. This PR does **not** claim a newer SDK migration.

Implementation decisions, all four persona effects, old-to-new regression coverage and precise native/IME evidence scope are maintained in [SPN-099.md](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/blob/f4e7db978a553a0dcc286937503de87b79ee9d06/docs/implementation/SPN-099.md).

### Failure dispositions and limits

The first runtime checkpoint `98bb7db` ([CI run](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41326551744)) exposed formatting/test-type errors, duplicate UI interceptor registration and over-broad paragraph history isolation. These were corrected in the current candidate; that failed run is not counted as final acceptance. Its four library partitions passed, while Unit and browser gates correctly rejected the checkpoint.

Two new adversarial fixtures reproduced pre-existing stock behavior outside captured native producer shapes: arbitrary paragraph-style COVER and a combined paragraph/comment REPLACE. Maintained tests document the native producer boundary and retain an explicit stock/adapted negative control. No original regression or supported producer obligation was dropped. The existing collapsed-drawing visibility limitation remains documented separately from saved geometry/reopen preservation. Native deletion and QuickList can emit COVER paragraph metadata; the adapter preserves those native paths. The documented scope no longer describes COVER as deletion-only.

No retries, seed reductions, expected-history changes or workflow waivers were introduced.

### Retained drawing and upstream acceptance

The CI artifact allowlist now explicitly retains `retained-drawing-*.png` and `retained-drawing-*.json`; the seven stage screenshots use that common prefix. This closes the evidence-upload gap without changing assertions, timing, retries or scheduling. All nine emitted filenames were checked against the exact two upload patterns, and narrow formatting passed (0.57 s / 162.5 MiB).

Two browser cases, for widths **0** and **-20**, run in both existing sync-development and sync-production projects. They use native-seeded imported PNG resources, a positive-size control using the same source, and actual renderer pixel assertions. They cover owner/peer sheet activation, switching away and back, edits and synchronization, full browser reload/reopen, exact saved drawing-resource preservation, and absence of resync/page errors. Failure artifacts include screenshots, pixel counts, native resources, and existing sync diagnostics.

A native placement diagnostic found that the initial positive-control seeds were not yet canonical: first refresh added native defaults and header-offset coordinates. This candidate now seeds only the two positive controls through the public placement API and the real native sheet skeleton. The collapsed seeds and every canvas, complete-resource, editing and sync assertion remain unchanged. The corrected exact-helper diagnostic proves both positive controls are byte-stable on their first and second native refresh while collapsed entries are still rejected and preserved.

The exact fixture/import/refresh path passed locally. Actual browser execution is pending hosted CI: the pinned local Chromium revision was unavailable, and the official CDN returned a 195-byte HTML “Site Unavailable” response instead of the ZIP. No substitute browser or reduced assertion was used.

Independent source reviews identified the missing upstream submission, distinct renderer acceptance, a stale README claim, and overbroad producer/slicing wording. The submission and wording are now corrected; the new browser cases supply the missing executable renderer check. Final review scoring awaits current-head evidence.

Upstream #7987 has passed ESLint, all four test shards, and the test aggregate. Its build and typecheck have also passed.
